item.title: More than 5000 grade ten students sit for final exam in Madang
item.description: A total of 5,145 nominated grade ten students are writing their final examination papers in Madang Province this week. Provincial Education Director Alphonse Igag explained these are students who have been issued their candidate's number by the Department of Education.
item.content:encoded:
A total of 5,145 nominated grade ten students are writing their final examination papers in Madang Province this week.

Provincial Education Director Alphonse Igag explained these are students who have been issued their candidate's number by the Department of Education.

Mr Igag said that despite the ongoing El Nino period, the grade ten examination is time bound, and there is no alternative but to start today, Monday 5th October.

"This is a fixed activity, so despite the challenges posed by El Nino and the unavailability of examination funds, the examinations still proceed. Madang Province has 36 secondary and high schools sitting the 2026 National Grade 10 Examinations," he said.

He said districts like Middle Ramu and Gama Local Level Government in Usino/ Bundi, which do not have road connection to the provincial capital, their leaders have hired helicopters to airlift the examination materials to their schools.

"The Madang Provincial Education authorities acknowledge the support of the Member for Middle, Kansol Harwai Kamdaru and his District Development Authority for the ongoing support over the years towards the successful delivery of examinations to grades 10 and 12 students during this time of the year.

"We also extend our gratitude to other MPs and their DDAs for their support as well.

The Madang Provincial Examinations Supervisor for Grade 10 Examinations, Darren Seming has kept school principals well informed of Examinations dates, collection and distribution of examination packages, supervision arrangements between neighboring schools and collection of examination papers after the completion, and dates to return the examination scripts.

School principals have responded positively and have ensured that examination papers have been stored in secured places before commencing today.

Mr Igag said the Education Division does not anticipate any major hiccups to the start of the examinations.

"We wish every grade 10 student in Madang Province and throughout PNG every success in the 2026 National Grade 10 Examinations," he added.

item.title: Hela parents urged to prioritize children’s education
item.description: Parents across Hela Province, particularly fathers, have been strongly urged to shift their financial priorities away from costly community expectations and focus instead on investing in their children's education. ​The call was made by John Tipa, a board member of Hela Education Services and the Provincial Election Manager, who cautioned that spending valuable resources on traditional obligations
item.content:encoded:
Parents across Hela Province, particularly fathers, have been strongly urged to shift their financial priorities away from costly community expectations and focus instead on investing in their children's education.

​The call was made by John Tipa, a board member of Hela Education Services and the Provincial Election Manager, who cautioned that spending valuable resources on traditional obligations solely to gain social standing yields no long-term security.

​Mr. Tipa emphasized that significant sums of money are routinely funneled into community events, such as house cries, funeral gatherings, compensation demands, and social contributions at the expense of basic educational needs.

​"Parents, especially fathers, like to contribute heavily to funeral services, compensation, and other community obligations," Mr. Tipa stated. "That money and those resources spent unnecessarily should be spent on their children's needs, such as clothing and school supplies."

He pointed out that while traditional contributions may offer fleeting social prestige, educating children provides a sustainable safety net for parents in their later years. Furthermore, he noted that building a generation of educated local professionals is essential for driving economic growth and social progress across Hela Province and Papua New Guinea.

​While acknowledging the provincial government's efforts under Governor Philip Undialu to subsidize school fees and upgrade educational infrastructure, Tipa stressed that public intervention must be met with equal commitment at home.

​"When the government is doing so much for the students, parents must also do their part and not depend on everything from the government," he warned, calling on parents to eliminate dependency and take full accountability for their households.

"Parents must not be lazy and dependent; they are responsible for their children's education," he said.

​Mr. Tipa challenged parents across the province to step up as responsible guardians by making their children’s academic future their ultimate priority.

item.title: Joy Korua farewelled after 43 years in teaching
item.description: The longest-serving teacher at St Mary’s Komkui primary school, Rose Joy Korua, has been farewell after giving 43 years of her life to teaching. Mrs. Korua spent 41 years in St Mary's Komkui primary school and another two years teaching in Southern Highlands.
item.content:encoded:
The longest-serving teacher at St Mary’s Komkui primary school, Rose Joy Korua, has been farewell after giving 43 years of her life to teaching.

Mrs. Korua spent 41 years in St Mary's Komkui primary school and another two years teaching in Southern Highlands.

Her farewell at the school last week was attended by Hagen Open MP William Duma, Western Highlands Governor Wai Rapa, former students, and community leaders.

The school gave Mrs. Korua a colorful farewell, with students and teachers singing and dancing to mark the end of her long teaching journey.

The celebrations also brought emotional moments as Mrs. Korua said goodbye to the school where she had spent most of her teaching years.

Hagen Open MP William Duma acknowledged Mrs. Korua for her service to education, especially in the Hagen Open electorate.

Duma said her farewell was well deserved and presented K10,000 to Mrs. Korua on behalf of the Mt Hagen City Authority (MHCA).

“Mrs. Korua has served our people for many years, especially through education. Her service is deserving of recognition, and we thank her for what she has done," Duma said.

The Western Highlands Provincial Government also presented a similar gesture to Mrs. Korua.

Governor Wai Rapa said teachers like Mrs. Korua have helped build and strengthen education in the province by producing people who are now serving Western Highlands and Papua New Guinea.

St Mary’s Komkui primary school headteacher Mr. Apa also thanked Mrs. Korua for her years of service.

“We thank Mrs. Korua for her outstanding service to this school. She has given many years to teaching our children, and we will always remember her contribution," Mr. Apa said.

One of her former students, now a practicing lawyer, Bobby Nutley, also returned to honor Mrs. Korua and the other teachers who taught him.

Nutley said the dedication of teachers can be seen in the lives of their former students.

“Teachers like Mrs. Korua gave up their lives to teach us. Today, we can see the results of their work in the lives of the students who have passed through this school," Mr. Nutley added.

He encouraged people in the community to continue pursuing education and to make sure their children also have access to school.

“Education is the key to everything. We must continue to educate ourselves and also make sure our children get the opportunity to go to school.”

For Mrs. Korua, the farewell marked the end of a long journey that began more than four decades ago.

An emotional Mrs. Korua thanked God and everyone who had been part of her 43 years in teaching.

She said she was leaving with a good heart and mind, knowing that her contribution to education had not been wasted.

“I thank the Good Lord and everyone who has been part of my journey for these 43 years. I am leaving with a good heart and a good mind, knowing that my contribution to education has not gone to waste," retired teacher Mrs. Korua said.

Mrs. Korua leaves behind generations of students who have gone on to become professionals, leaders, parents, and community members.

Her 43 years in teaching have now come to an end, but her contribution to the education of Western Highlands and Papua New Guinea will remain through the many lives she has touched.

item.title: PNG pushes to open Yetetkun border for El Nino relief
item.description: Western Province is pushing for the opening of the Yetetkun border to allow food supplies into drought-affected communities in North and Middle Fly. This was highlighted during a high-level border inspection last Friday at Yetetkun, on the PNG-Indonesia border.
item.content:encoded:
Western Province is pushing for the opening of the Yetetkun border to allow food supplies into drought-affected communities in North and Middle Fly.

This was highlighted during a high-level border inspection last Friday at Yetetkun, on the PNG-Indonesia border.

A delegation comprising of OTML and CIQS representatives from Port Moresby, led by Head of Delegation, Foreign Affairs Acting Director General for Asia Region, Mr Samson Yabon, flew from Port Moresby to Merauke and travelled by road to Yetetkun.

The team was hosted by Indonesian Consul General in Vanimo, Mr Tangkuman Alexander.

Western Provincial Administrator Robert Kaiyun travelled from Kiunga, crossing the Alice River to join the meeting.

Mr Kaiyun reaffirmed the province's support to open the border and called for an Indonesian Consulate to be established in Kiunga to strengthen ties.

He said improved road access must support the El Niño response, particularly delivery of basic food supplies.

Meanwhile, DPLLGA Director for Border Affairs Jacqueline Winuan announced that registration for Traditional Border Crosser Cards will begin in Ambaga and surrounding villages within the next two weeks to support legitimate trade and movement.

Supporting the Provincial Administrator were representatives from DPLLGA, PNGDF, the North Fly Police Command, Provincial Customs, Immigration, Quarantine and Security (CIQS) agencies, and senior officers of the Western Provincial Administration.

item.title: Governor Bird warns public servants against stealing
item.description: East Sepik Governor Allan Bird has warned public servants allegedly involved in the misuse or theft of public funds that they could face police investigation and imprisonment. Governor Bird issued the warning during graduation ceremonies at Brugam SSEC Secondary School in Maprik on Thursday 1st October and Maprik Secondary School and Bob Spence Technical High School at Kusambuk, Yangoru-Saussia, o
item.content:encoded:
East Sepik Governor Allan Bird has warned public servants allegedly involved in the misuse or theft of public funds that they could face police investigation and imprisonment.

Governor Bird issued the warning during graduation ceremonies at Brugam SSEC Secondary School in Maprik on Thursday 1st October and Maprik Secondary School and Bob Spence Technical High School at Kusambuk, Yangoru-Saussia, on Friday 2nd of October.

“The practice of Sepiks sitting in position and stealing from our own people must stop,” Mr Bird told graduates, parents, teachers and community members.

He said he had commissioned an audit of the East Sepik Provincial Administration and was awaiting the completed report.

“I told our Provincial Police Commander that I want those who steal from the people to go to jail,” he said.

Governor Bird said one of the major challenges facing his administration was alleged collusion between some public servants and businessmen, which he claimed was resulting in public money being diverted from projects intended to benefit communities.

He cited a school project in Wosera-Gawi as an example, alleging that a contractor had walked away from the project after funds were allegedly taken through collusion with public servants based in Wewak.

“I can assure you that the police are hunting down people right now and they will go to jail,” he said.

“I am sick and tired of public servants colluding with bad people and stealing from you.”

He said the issue was particularly serious because provincial governments were facing increasing pressure on their available funding.

He said if provincial governments were receiving less funding, the limited resources available must be properly managed and directed to essential services and development projects.

“We must not misuse the money or steal from it and wait for the next funding,” he said.

The Governor's comments came amid his broader call for greater accountability within the provincial administration, with the audit expected to provide a clearer picture of how public funds have been managed.

He said his administration would continue to pursue those responsible for allegedly misusing public resources.

Bird made the remarks during a two-day visit to the Maprik and Yangoru-Saussia areas, where he attended the three graduation ceremonies and officially opened the Kusaun and Miko rural markets along the main Sepik Highway.

The Governor's allegations concerning the Wosera-Gawi school project and other possible cases of misuse of public funds have yet to be tested in court. The outcome of the provincial administration audit and any police investigation will determine whether individuals will face criminal charges.

item.title: Family of late Dr. Waiye unhappy over delay
item.description: The family of the late Dr. Robert Waiye has expressed dissatisfaction after his murder case was further deferred to Wednesday, despite being directed for a second mention today by the presiding Magistrate. Relatives of the late doctor arrived at the Kundiawa District Court this morning for what was expected to be the second mention as directed by the Magistrate last Friday.
item.content:encoded:
The family of the late Dr. Robert Waiye has expressed dissatisfaction after his murder case was further deferred to Wednesday, despite being directed for a second mention today by the presiding Magistrate.

Relatives of the late doctor arrived at the Kundiawa District Court this morning for what was expected to be the second mention as directed by the Magistrate last Friday.

However, police requested the matter be adjourned to Wednesday to correct errors in the information laid before the court.

Apa Dama, representing the relatives of the late Dr. Waiye, pointed out errors in the police information, where the late doctor's name was misspelled as "Waine" instead of Waiye, and his origin was incorrectly written as "Sinasina-Yongomugl Province" instead of Sinasina-Yongomugl District.

Mr. Dama said they respect the law and have placed everything under the law, but such errors and delays were disappointing.

"We have lost a son who came to serve his own people, but we are still respecting the law. All we ask is for police to be serious and do their job properly," Mr. Dama said.

In response, Simbu Provincial Police Commander, Detective Superintendent Mazuc Rubiang, assured the family that all errors since Friday have now been corrected and the seven suspects have been charged under one offence.

He said by Wednesday the court will hear the matter into the death of Dr. Waiye.

PPC Rubiang commended the family for their patience and appealed for their continued cooperation, saying together they will ensure justice is served.

He also confirmed that Dr. Ronald Conn, who accompanied Dr. Waiye on the night of the incident, was charged today and will also appear on Wednesday.

The late Dr. Waiye, 26, from Gera village in Sinasina-Yongomugl District, died on September 16 after allegedly being assaulted at Gateway Fuelers at Prenorka on the night of September 15. Seven suspects remain in custody.

item.title: 200 students graduate at Wawin National High
item.description: Wawin National High School graduated 200 students at their school ground, outside Lae, in Wampar LLG of Morobe Province. Of the 200, 2 are students from Aiyura National High, who were in Wawin for studies, under some arrangements that have completed the year, successfully.
item.content:encoded:
Wawin National High School graduated 200 students at their school ground, outside Lae, in Wampar LLG of Morobe Province.

Of the 200, 2 are students from Aiyura National High, who were in Wawin for studies, under some arrangements that have completed the year, successfully.

During the graduation, Education Minister, Francis Kikin Siune, encouraged the graduates to follow their dreams, despite any setbacks in life.

MP Suine said, "after you walk out of those Wawin gates, the education doesnt stop there, you must not lose hope if results don't turn out as expected, but you must keep on pressing."

Education Secretary Dr. Uke Kombra present also at the event, alerted the students of the road to success. Dr Kombra said, " the road to success will have alot of challenges that you might encounter, but if you are focused and if you're always positive, then as Minster as mentioned, you can achieve your dream or you can become successful, in the respective careers you take in life. "

The National Education Development presented a cheque of K3m to the school and commited an extra million, to be paid later.

This is to serve the purpose of building more infrastructure to serve students learning in the school.

The same is also done to other 6 National High Schools in the country.

item.title: 31 years in the classroom: A teacher’s legacy lives on
item.description: The face may have changed with the passing years, but the voice is often familiar. For Ms Kulawi Buni, such unexpected encounters with former students—in banks, hospitals, airports and other places—have become some of the most treasured moments of her 31-year teaching career.
item.content:encoded:
The face may have changed with the passing years, but the voice is often familiar.

For Ms Kulawi Buni, such unexpected encounters with former students—in banks, hospitals, airports and other places—have become some of the most treasured moments of her 31-year teaching career.

As the world marks World Teachers’ Day on October 5, Ms Buni’s story offers a glimpse into the lasting impact teachers can have long after their students leave the classroom.

Now teaching at Zifasing Junior High School in Wampar, Huon Gulf District, Ms Buni has spent more than three decades serving in the education sector.

Her career has taken her across several provinces and regions of Papua New Guinea, including the Eastern Highlands, West New Britain, East New Britain, the Autonomous Region of Bougainville and her home province of Morobe.

Across those postings, she has taught generations of students who have since taken different paths in life.

Today, some of those former students are professionals working in banks, hospitals and other institutions. For Ms Buni, seeing them succeed is one of the greatest rewards of being a teacher.

But it is often the unexpected encounters that mean the most.

A former student recognising her in a public place, approaching her with gratitude or simply reminding her of the role she played during their school years is a powerful reminder that the work of a teacher extends far beyond the classroom.

For Ms Buni, those moments make the long years of teaching worthwhile.

Her 31-year journey has not simply been about delivering lessons or completing the school year. It has been about nurturing young people, encouraging them to believe in themselves and preparing them for life beyond school.

“I love moulding and shaping the elites of our great nation, Papua New Guinea,” she says.

Her words capture what has kept her committed to the profession for more than three decades.

For teachers like Ms Buni, success is not measured only by examination results or academic achievements. Sometimes, it comes years later, when a former student walks up, remembers their teacher and says thank you.

On October 5, World Teachers’ Day, her story is a reminder that while students may leave the classroom, the influence of a dedicated teacher can remain with them for a lifetime.

item.title: West Sepik rolls out mass drug administration and immunization campaign
item.description: The West Sepik Provincial Health Authority (WSPHA) will roll out its Mass Drug Administration (MDA) on Neglected Tropical Diseases (NTD) and Intensified Routine Immunization (IRI) campaign from October to November 2026, after officially launching it in Vanimo last Friday.
